title: Bug: test_bgp_update_timer.py fails due to TSA maintenance mode
author: saravanan-nexthop
body:
### Is it platform specific

generic

### Importance or Severity

Medium

### Description of the bug

test_bgp_update_timer.py teardown calls config_reload, which restarts swss. If the platform is enabled with startup_tsa_tsb.service in services.conf, swss.sh restarts this service on every non-warm-boot, putting the DUT into TSA maintenance mode with a 15-minute TSB timer. That causes the tests that run before the timer fires to fail because PfxSnt: 1 (only loopback advertised).

### Steps to Reproduce

test_bgp_update_timer.py run in 202511 on NH-5010 or similar platforms where TSA is enabled via startup-tsa-tsb.conf and services.conf in the /usr/share/sonic/platform directory. 

### Actual Behavior and Expected Behavior

The test passes when TSA maintenance mode doesn't kick in during the test's config reload. 

### Relevant log output

```shell

                    duthost.shell(
```

> [@saravanan-nexthop](https://github.com/saravanan-nexthop) this should have been handled by pre-test. Our expected model of manual test is that one should run pre-test once and then run individual tests.
> 
> A protection is great to have.
> 
> There are 2 PRs try to address the same issue. We need to pick one to keep.

@yxieca Arvind's comment in the PR23371 helped to identify that the pretest doesn't happen always. 
I wonder if we can have some pre-checks in the sonic-mgmt/tests/conftest.py that can catch the dut is not in a good state for any test to run and warn about it much earlier. This avoids debugging the test failure symptoms and going in wrong direction and then eventually finding out that dut wasn't in the correct state for the test to start running.

linkedPullRequests.title: [bgp] Clear TSA maintenance mode after config reload in test_bgp_update_timer
linkedPullRequests.author: rustiqly
linkedPullRequests.body:
## Description
On platforms with `startup_tsa_tsb` service enabled in `services.conf`, `config_reload` (from `setup_interfaces`) restarts swss which triggers TSA maintenance mode with a 15-minute TSB timer. Tests running before the timer fires fail because the DUT only advertises its loopback route (PfxSnt: 1).

### Fix
Check for TSA maintenance mode in `common_setup_teardown` before yielding to tests, and run `TSB` to clear it if active. Uses `TSC` to check current maintenance state.

### Changes
- `tests/bgp/test_bgp_update_timer.py`: Add TSA check/clear in `common_setup_teardown` fixture setup

Fixes: #23336

comments.author: rustiqly
comments.body:
Thanks for the review @saravanan-nexthop! 

I considered skip/assert but went with TSB for a few reasons:

1. **The TSA state is a side-effect, not a precondition** — it happens because `config_reload` (from `setup_interfaces`) restarts swss, which triggers the `startup_tsa_tsb` service. The test itself doesn't require TSA, it's just an artifact of the test setup.

2. **Skipping would hide valid test coverage** — the test_bgp_update_timer tests work fine once TSA is cleared. Skipping would mean these tests never run on platforms with `startup_tsa_tsb` enabled.

3. **Users running pretests may still hit this** — the issue is specifically triggered by `config_reload` within the fixture, so even after pretests, the fixture's own reload can re-trigger TSA.

The TSB approach is essentially "clean up what our fixture broke" rather than "bail out because something unexpected happened." Happy to discuss further if you see a downside!
